description: Concurrent use significantly increases bleeding risk. Aspirin inhibits platelet aggregation while warfarin inhibits clotting factors; together they produce additive hemorrhagic risk including life-threatening GI and intracranial bleeding.
recommendation: Avoid combination unless under strict specialist supervision. If both are required (e.g. mechanical heart valve with AF) use lowest effective aspirin dose and monitor INR frequently.

description: NSAIDs such as ibuprofen inhibit platelet function and cause GI mucosal damage; they also displace warfarin from plasma proteins and inhibit its metabolism via CYP2C9 raising INR unpredictably.
recommendation: Avoid concurrent use. Use paracetamol for analgesia where possible. If an NSAID is essential add a PPI and monitor INR closely.

description: Dual antiplatelet therapy increases bleeding risk significantly versus either agent alone. Although used intentionally in some ACS/stent patients the combination requires careful risk-benefit assessment.
recommendation: Use dual antiplatelet therapy only when clinically indicated (e.g. post-PCI). Limit duration and co-prescribe a PPI to reduce GI bleeding risk.

description: Alcohol inhibits gluconeogenesis and increases lactic acid production. Combined with metformin this raises the risk of lactic acidosis particularly with binge drinking and in patients with hepatic impairment.
recommendation: Advise patients to limit alcohol to moderate levels and avoid binge drinking. Monitor for signs of lactic acidosis (myalgia; weakness; abdominal pain).

description: Clarithromycin is a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor. It markedly increases atorvastatin plasma concentrations raising the risk of myopathy and potentially rhabdomyolysis with acute kidney injury.
recommendation: Avoid concurrent use where possible. If antibiotic therapy is necessary consider using azithromycin (weaker CYP3A4 effect) and temporarily withhold atorvastatin during the course.

description: Clarithromycin substantially increases simvastatin AUC by >10-fold via CYP3A4 inhibition creating very high risk of rhabdomyolysis.
recommendation: Withhold simvastatin during clarithromycin treatment. Switch to pravastatin or rosuvastatin if statin therapy must continue during the antibiotic course.

description: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4 and CYP2C9 thereby increasing warfarin exposure. It also reduces vitamin K-producing gut flora. INR may rise sharply and unpredictably.
recommendation: Monitor INR very closely during and for 1-2 weeks after clarithromycin treatment. Empirical dose reduction of warfarin may be necessary.

description: NSAIDs reduce renal prostaglandin synthesis causing sodium and water retention which increases renal tubular reabsorption of lithium leading to toxic serum lithium levels.
recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs in lithium-treated patients. Use paracetamol for analgesia. If an NSAID must be used reduce lithium dose; monitor serum lithium levels frequently and watch for toxicity signs.

description: Loop diuretics cause sodium and volume depletion triggering compensatory lithium reabsorption in the proximal tubule and raising serum lithium to toxic levels.
recommendation: If a loop diuretic is necessary reduce lithium dose and monitor serum levels frequently. Ensure adequate sodium intake and watch for toxicity symptoms.

description: Amiodarone inhibits P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 substantially increasing digoxin plasma concentrations and risk of toxicity (bradycardia; heart block; arrhythmia).
recommendation: Reduce digoxin dose by 30-50% when amiodarone is introduced. Monitor digoxin serum levels and ECG. This interaction persists for weeks after amiodarone discontinuation due to its long half-life.

description: NSAIDs reduce renal clearance of methotrexate by competing for tubular secretion leading to methotrexate toxicity (myelosuppression; mucositis; nephrotoxicity).
recommendation: Avoid concurrent NSAID use with methotrexate especially at higher doses used in oncology. If necessary in low-dose rheumatological regimens monitor closely and ensure adequate hydration.

description: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19 reducing the metabolic activation of clopidogrel (a prodrug) by up to 45% thereby diminishing its antiplatelet effect and potentially increasing cardiovascular risk.
recommendation: Prefer pantoprazole or lansoprazole over omeprazole or esomeprazole if a PPI is required alongside clopidogrel. Consider the patient's overall CV risk when selecting GI prophylaxis.

description: Fluoxetine inhibits CYP2D6 blocking tramadol activation and also adds serotonergic load. Combination risks both serotonin syndrome (agitation; hyperthermia; myoclonus) and reduced tramadol analgesia.
recommendation: Avoid combination. If an SNRI/SSRI is needed alongside an opioid consider a non-serotonergic opioid such as morphine or oxycodone with close monitoring.

description: Tramadol inhibits serotonin reuptake; combined with sertraline this creates additive serotonergic stimulation with risk of serotonin syndrome. CYP2D6 inhibition by sertraline also alters tramadol metabolism.
recommendation: Avoid concurrent use. Monitor closely for serotonin syndrome symptoms: tremor; agitation; sweating; tachycardia; hyperthermia. Use alternative analgesic if possible.

description: Fluconazole is a potent CYP2C9 inhibitor. Even a single dose can double or triple warfarin exposure causing dangerous INR elevation and bleeding.
recommendation: Monitor INR very closely when fluconazole is prescribed. Anticipate INR rise within 1-2 days and reduce warfarin dose proactively. Monitor until INR is stable after completing fluconazole course.

description: Both drugs are CYP3A4/CYP2C9 inducers. They reduce each other's plasma levels unpredictably making seizure control difficult. Some metabolic pathways may be inhibited raising toxicity risk.
recommendation: Monitor serum levels of both drugs closely when used together. Combination is sometimes unavoidable in refractory epilepsy; specialist neurology guidance is recommended.

description: Carbamazepine induces the metabolism of valproate reducing its levels. Valproate inhibits the epoxidation of carbamazepine's active metabolite (carbamazepine-10 11-epoxide) increasing toxicity.
recommendation: Monitor levels and clinical response for both drugs. Watch for carbamazepine toxicity signs (diplopia; dizziness) and ensure adequate valproate levels for seizure control.

description: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2 and reduces vitamin K production by gut flora leading to significantly elevated INR and bleeding risk.
recommendation: Monitor INR 2-3 days after starting ciprofloxacin and adjust warfarin dose accordingly. Inform patients of bleeding signs and symptoms.

description: Metronidazole inhibits CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 substantially increasing warfarin exposure. It also reduces gut flora vitamin K synthesis. INR can increase 2-3 fold.
recommendation: Reduce warfarin dose empirically by ~25-50% when metronidazole is prescribed. Monitor INR every 2-3 days during treatment and for 1 week after completion.

description: Azithromycin reduces intestinal flora vitamin K synthesis and may have a mild CYP interaction raising INR.
recommendation: Monitor INR during and shortly after the azithromycin course. May require temporary warfarin dose adjustment.

description: Combining potassium-sparing agents (spironolactone) with ACE inhibitors (lisinopril) significantly increases risk of hyperkalaemia which can cause fatal cardiac arrhythmia.
recommendation: Monitor serum potassium and renal function within 1-2 weeks of combining and periodically thereafter. Avoid in CKD. Use in heart failure is beneficial but requires vigilant monitoring.

description: ARBs and potassium-sparing diuretics both reduce aldosterone-mediated potassium excretion creating additive hyperkalaemia risk.
recommendation: Monitor potassium and renal function closely. Combination is used in heart failure under specialist supervision. Avoid in significant renal impairment.

description: Both furosemide and aminoglycosides are independently ototoxic and nephrotoxic. Concurrent use markedly increases risk of permanent hearing loss and acute kidney injury.
recommendation: Avoid concurrent use where possible. If both are required use minimum effective doses; monitor renal function and audiological function; ensure adequate hydration.

description: Clarithromycin is a potent CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibitor. It dramatically increases colchicine plasma levels potentially causing fatal colchicine toxicity (multi-organ failure; bone marrow suppression).
recommendation: This combination is potentially fatal. Avoid in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. If unavoidable use the absolute minimum colchicine dose for the shortest period with close monitoring.

description: Allopurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase which is the primary metabolic route for azathioprine. This causes azathioprine to accumulate to toxic levels producing severe myelosuppression.
recommendation: Reduce azathioprine dose by 75% when allopurinol is added. Monitor FBC very frequently. Consider alternative urate-lowering therapy to avoid this critical interaction.

description: Carbamazepine is a potent CYP2C9 inducer that significantly reduces warfarin plasma levels making anticoagulation inadequate and predisposing to thromboembolic events.
recommendation: Monitor INR closely when carbamazepine is started or stopped. Warfarin dose increases of 50-100% are often required. Be alert to INR falling when carbamazepine is added.

description: Phenytoin induces CYP2C9 reducing warfarin levels and reducing anticoagulation efficacy. However at initiation phenytoin may transiently displace warfarin and raise INR.
recommendation: Monitor INR closely throughout phenytoin therapy. Expect need to increase warfarin dose. Be vigilant for both under- and over-anticoagulation.

description: Rifampicin is one of the most potent CYP inducers known. It can reduce warfarin levels by 80-90% virtually abolishing anticoagulation in standard doses.
recommendation: If rifampicin is essential dramatically increase warfarin dose (often 3-5 fold) and monitor INR every few days. When rifampicin is stopped reduce warfarin dose immediately to avoid haemorrhage.

description: Amiodarone inhibits CYP2C9 substantially increasing warfarin levels. Due to amiodarone's extremely long half-life (weeks to months) the interaction is prolonged and cumulative.
recommendation: Reduce warfarin dose by ~30-50% when amiodarone is commenced. Monitor INR very closely for months. Even after stopping amiodarone monitor INR for 1-3 months.

description: Iodinated contrast media can cause acute kidney injury. Reduced renal clearance then allows metformin accumulation creating risk of lactic acidosis.
recommendation: Withhold metformin for 48 hours before and after procedures involving iodinated contrast media in patients with eGFR <60. Reassess renal function before restarting.

description: SSRIs inhibit platelet serotonin uptake reducing platelet aggregation. NSAIDs inhibit platelet cyclooxygenase. Combined they significantly increase GI bleeding risk.
recommendation: Co-prescribe a PPI when an SSRI and NSAID must be used together. Consider alternative analgesia. Monitor for GI bleeding symptoms.

description: SGLT-2 inhibitors increase urinary glucose and sodium excretion and cause modest volume depletion. Adding a loop diuretic amplifies volume depletion with risk of dehydration hypotension and AKI.
recommendation: Monitor volume status renal function and blood pressure when combining. Patients should maintain adequate hydration. Consider temporary dose reduction of diuretic.

description: Alcohol inhibits hepatic gluconeogenesis and impairs counter-regulatory response to hypoglycaemia. Combined with insulin this prolongs and worsens hypoglycaemic episodes.
recommendation: Counsel patients to eat when drinking alcohol. Monitor blood glucose closely. Warn about difficulty recognising hypoglycaemia symptoms with alcohol. Avoid heavy alcohol consumption.

description: Cimetidine inhibits renal tubular secretion of metformin by competing for the OCT2 transporter increasing metformin plasma levels and risk of lactic acidosis.
recommendation: Prefer ranitidine or a PPI over cimetidine in patients taking metformin. If cimetidine is required monitor renal function and watch for metformin toxicity signs.

description: Loop diuretics can cause electrolyte changes and volume depletion that may modestly affect glycaemic control in diabetic patients though direct pharmacokinetic interaction is minimal.
recommendation: Monitor blood glucose more closely when initiating or changing loop diuretic therapy. Adjust antidiabetic therapy if glycaemic control deteriorates.

description: Both venlafaxine (SNRI) and tramadol (weak SNRI plus opioid) inhibit serotonin reuptake. Combination creates significant risk of serotonin syndrome.
recommendation: Avoid concurrent use. If both are required use the lowest effective doses with close clinical monitoring for serotonin syndrome features. Have a low threshold to discontinue one agent.

description: Both corticosteroids and NSAIDs damage gastric mucosa and impair its protective mechanisms. Combination dramatically increases risk of peptic ulcer and GI bleeding.
recommendation: Prescribe a PPI as gastroprotection whenever this combination is required. Use NSAIDs for the shortest possible duration and at the lowest effective dose.

description: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4 increasing quetiapine plasma levels. Both drugs independently prolong QTc creating additive risk of serious ventricular arrhythmia (Torsades de Pointes).
recommendation: Avoid combination or monitor ECG closely if essential. Consider alternative antibiotic. If used together obtain baseline ECG and monitor QTc.

description: Clarithromycin increases risperidone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and QT prolongation is additive.
recommendation: Monitor for QT prolongation with ECG. Consider alternative antibiotic. Monitor for extrapyramidal side effects from elevated risperidone levels.

description: Furosemide causes hypokalaemia and hypomagnesaemia which sensitise the myocardium to digoxin toxicity even at therapeutic digoxin levels.
recommendation: Monitor electrolytes especially potassium and replace as needed. Monitor for signs of digoxin toxicity (nausea; bradycardia; visual disturbances). Maintain K+ >4 mmol/L.

description: Amlodipine mildly inhibits CYP3A4 increasing simvastatin plasma levels and myopathy risk. FDA advises simvastatin dose not to exceed 20 mg/day when combined with amlodipine.
recommendation: Limit simvastatin dose to 20 mg/day with amlodipine. Consider switching to rosuvastatin or pravastatin (not CYP3A4-dependent) if higher statin intensity is required.

description: MAO inhibitors combined with SSRIs cause serotonin syndrome which can be fatal. Serotonin accumulates to dangerous levels in central and peripheral synapses.
recommendation: This combination is absolutely contraindicated. Allow a 14-day washout after stopping an MAOI before starting fluoxetine. Due to fluoxetine's long half-life allow 5 weeks after stopping fluoxetine before starting an MAOI.

description: Calcium carbonate binds levothyroxine in the GI tract reducing its absorption by up to 25%. This can impair thyroid hormone replacement adequacy and cause hypothyroid symptoms.
recommendation: Separate administration of levothyroxine and calcium supplements by at least 4 hours. Take levothyroxine on an empty stomach. Monitor TSH when calcium supplementation is started or changed.

description: Divalent cations (Mg2+ Al3+ Ca2+) in antacids chelate ciprofloxacin in the gut reducing its oral bioavailability by up to 90%.
recommendation: Administer ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after antacid products. The same applies to iron and zinc supplements.

description: Dietary vitamin K is the direct pharmacological antagonist of warfarin. Sudden increases in vitamin K intake (e.g. from green leafy vegetables) reduce anticoagulation effect.
recommendation: Counsel patients to maintain a consistent dietary vitamin K intake. Avoid dramatic increases or decreases in consumption of green leafy vegetables (spinach; kale; broccoli). Monitor INR when diet changes.

description: Both albuterol (beta-2 agonist) and loop diuretics independently cause hypokalaemia. Concurrent use produces additive potassium depletion which may precipitate arrhythmias.
recommendation: Monitor serum potassium when high-dose nebulised albuterol is used in combination with loop diuretics. Consider potassium supplementation. Monitor ECG in high-risk patients.

description: Gabapentin combined with opioids produces additive CNS and respiratory depression. Multiple studies show this combination significantly increases mortality from respiratory depression.
recommendation: Avoid concurrent use where possible. If combination is necessary use the lowest effective doses of both. Provide naloxone to patient/caregiver. Counsel on risk; avoid alcohol and other CNS depressants.

description: Carbamazepine is a potent CYP3A4 inducer that reduces ethinylestradiol and progestogen plasma levels by up to 50% causing contraceptive failure and unintended pregnancy.
recommendation: Use additional non-hormonal contraception (e.g. condoms) throughout carbamazepine therapy. Consider long-acting non-hormonal contraception (copper IUD). Counsel all women of childbearing potential on this risk.

description: SGLT-2 inhibitors combined with insulin increase hypoglycaemia risk. Euglycaemic DKA is also a recognised rare but serious adverse effect of this combination.
recommendation: Reduce insulin dose by 20% when starting an SGLT-2 inhibitor. Monitor blood glucose closely. Educate patients on DKA symptoms and withhold dapagliflozin perioperatively.

description: Donepezil (acetylcholinesterase inhibitor) and anticholinergic agents are pharmacodynamic antagonists. Anticholinergics reduce donepezil efficacy for cognition; combination also produces unpredictable cholinergic effects.
recommendation: Avoid prescribing anticholinergic drugs to patients on donepezil. Conduct regular medication reviews for anticholinergic burden. The Anticholinergic Burden Scale can guide deprescribing.
